To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AII amacrine cell dendrites in the mouse and in the rat retina express connexin36.
Cx36 immunoreactivity in the inner puxiform layer is confined to sublamina a and is localized to AII amacrine cell dendrites and rod and cone bipolar cell axon terminals.
Cx36 expression in the mammalian retina is confined to AII amacrine, rod bipolar and cone bipolar cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of neuronal connexins in the mammalian retina and the functional implications of these gap junctions in retinal signal processing.
the role of Cx36 in retinal signal processing and with the functional properties of gap junctional communication in the retina.
the expression pattern of Cx36 in the mammalian retina.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Cx36 forms heterotypic gap junctions between AII amacrine cell processes and ON cone bipolar cell processes, whereas homotypic gap junctional contacts are found between AII amacrinic cell processes.
Cx36 expression in the IPL of the mammalian retina is restricted to dendrites of A II amacrines.
Cx36 in the mouse retina is expressed by A-type horizontal cells and AII amacrine cells and in gap junctions between them.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Cx36 in the mouse and the rat retina is expressed in AII amacrine, ON cone bipolar, and rod bipolar cells.
Cx36 forms gap junctions in the retina that are heterologous, heterotypic, and heterocellular.
AII amacrine neurons express Cx36 in the mammalian retina.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AII amacrine gap junctions are heterologous and heterotypic, and that they connect AII amacrine to ON cone bipolar cell dendrites.
the AII amacrine cell is a connexin36-positive cell type in the mammalian retina.
the expression pattern of Cx36 is highly conserved in mouse and rat retinas and that AII amacrine neurons express this connexin.
